page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Stress — the definition
lines: A deforming force sets up an
internal restoring force in a body.
Stress is this restoring force per
steps.margin_note: The words "restoring force per unit area" earn this mark — the formula alone does not.
steps.why: The restoring force equals the applied force only while the body is in equilibrium, so a problem's given force can be used to find the stress.
common_mistakes: Calling stress the applied force per unit area. Stress is the RESTORING force per unit area.
Leaving out "per unit area" and defining stress as just the restoring force.
steps.memory_tip: Stress = restoring force / area — the body pushes back, and stress measures that push-back over area.

steps.label: Formula and unit

lines.text: σ = F/A, SI unit N m⁻²

steps.margin_note: Give both the formula AND the unit — either alone earns only partial credit from most examiners.
steps.why: Stress has the same unit as pressure because both are a force divided by an area, so N m⁻² follows directly from the formula.
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as N m² instead of N m⁻².
Omitting the unit altogether after writing the formula.
steps.memory_tip: Force over area gives the same unit as pressure: N m⁻².
